decks.title: Introduction to AI and Data Science
Classification Part 1: Bayes Error and Metrics

questions.p: What does the Turing test evaluate?
o: Whether a program behaves indistinguishably from a human
The Turing test belongs to acting humanly: only behaviour is observed.
Whether a program solves logic problems correctly
Whether a program uses human reasoning steps internally
Whether a program improves with more training data

questions.p: Which capability lets a Turing-test program adapt to new circumstances and extrapolate patterns?
o: The slide assigns adapting and detecting patterns to machine learning.

questions.p: The syllogism "Socrates is a man; all men are mortal" is the classic example of which approach?
o: Laws of thought and syllogisms define thinking rationally, which initiated logic.

questions.p: A reflex that pulls your hand from a hot surface illustrates which point?
o: Rational agents must always reason logically first
Behaviour can be rational without careful deliberation
The slide uses it to show that logical thinking is only one part of appropriate behaviour.
Human reflexes cannot be modeled by any agent
Rationality requires explicit laws of thought

questions.p: Which statement about AI and machine learning is correct?
o: AI is one branch inside the field of machine learning
Machine learning is AI, but not all AI is machine learning
AI is the umbrella; ML is one of its branches.
AI and machine learning are two names for one field
All AI systems learn patterns from historical data

questions.p: How does machine learning differ from traditional programming?
o: It takes rules and answers and produces the data
It needs neither historical data nor expected answers
It takes data and answers and produces the rules
Data plus rules giving answers describes traditional programming.
It takes data and rules and produces the answers

questions.p: A set of JSON records from a web API is best classified as:
o: JSON has keys and nesting without a fixed tabular schema.

questions.p: A sensor feed that delivers thousands of readings every second mainly illustrates which Big Data challenge?
o: Velocity is the speed at which data is generated.

questions.p: A dataset contains conflicting and unreliable records. Which V is the concern?
o: Veracity is uncertainty about data quality.

questions.p: In the slide's process, what comes immediately after data cleaning?
o: The order is collection, cleaning, exploration, feature engineering, building, evaluation, deployment.

questions.p: What is the main purpose of exploratory data analysis?
o: To understand data characteristics before modeling
The slide states EDA's purpose directly.
To compute the final accuracy of a model
To deploy a trained model into production
To replace data cleaning with visual checks

questions.p: A retailer forecasts next quarter's demand using past sales. This is:
o: It estimates what will happen. Recommending an order size would be prescriptive.

questions.p: A ride-hailing app picks which driver to send to each customer. This is:
o: It recommends the action to take.

questions.p: Which description matches a Pandas Series?
o: A DataFrame is the two-dimensional table; each of its columns is a Series.
A list of DataFrames stored by key
A connection to a SQL table

questions.p: What is the index of pd.Series({"a": 10, "b": 20})?
o: No index until one is assigned

questions.p: How many values does pd.Series(5, index=[0, 1, 2, 3]) contain?
o: A scalar is repeated once for every index label.

questions.p: For a Series with default index, what does s[1:4] return?
o: Only the elements at positions 1 and 4

questions.p: For labels a to e, what does s["a":"c"] return?
o: The elements labeled b and c
Only the elements labeled a and c
The elements labeled a, b and c
Label slices include the end label.
The elements labeled a and b

questions.p: What does df[["Name", "Age"]] return?
o: A DataFrame with those two columns
A list of columns returns a DataFrame.
The first two rows of the table

questions.p: Which filter is written correctly?
o: Use & with parentheses around each condition.

questions.p: What does df.iloc[:3, 1:3] select?
o: Rows labeled 3 and columns labeled 1 to 3
iloc uses integer positions with exclusive ends.

questions.p: Which read_csv parameter loads only certain columns?
What does pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name=None) return?
o: A dictionary of DataFrames, one per sheet
The slide says None reads all sheets into a dictionary.
Only the last sheet as a DataFrame
Only the first sheet as a DataFrame

questions.p: JSON shaped as a list of row dictionaries matches which orient?
o: records means a list of dictionaries, one per row.

questions.p: Which if_exists value adds new rows to an existing SQL table?
o: replace drops the table, and fail raises an error.

questions.p: Which call writes newline-delimited JSON?
o: lines=True is only valid with orient="records".

questions.p: In the nutrition data, "situation" (living alone, as a couple, with family) is best described as:
o: A design variable that defines a group
It describes which group a person belongs to, not a measured outcome.
An identifier column for each row
A measurement that varies per person

questions.p: Why is header=None passed when reading abalone.data?
o: The file is not comma separated
It makes column names come from row 2
The file has no row of column names
Without it, Pandas treats the first data row as headers.
It removes the first row of data

questions.p: The number of births in a hospital per day is:
o: A count has a countable set of possible values.

questions.p: Eye color with values blue, black, brown and green is:
o: It has a fixed set of categories with no numeric meaning.

questions.p: Why did Python treat all 13 nutri features as quantitative at first?
o: They were entered as whole numbers
Category codes were stored as integers.
The file had no column names to read
read_excel always converts text to integers

questions.p: Which line correctly recodes gender?
o: replace maps codes to labels; astype sets the type.

questions.p: What does describe report for a categorical column?
o: The numeric summary applies only to quantitative features.

questions.p: What does margins=True add to pd.crosstab?
o: It adds the All row and column.

questions.p: The 0.75 sample quantile is also called:
o: 25, 50 and 75 percentiles are the first, second and third quartiles.

questions.p: If the sample variance is 81, what is the standard deviation?
o: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

questions.p: Which plot should show how height relates to weight?
To compare coffee consumption between men and women, use:
o: One qualitative and one quantitative variable.

questions.p: Forward fill is best suited to:
o: It uses the neighbouring value, which needs a meaningful order.

questions.p: Which expression gives the number of missing values per column?
o: True counts as 1, so sum counts the missing entries.

questions.p: Students who registered late have no Major 1 score because they had not yet taken it. This is:
o: The missingness depends on other observed data, the registration date.

questions.p: A student who failed the final deliberately skips submitting it. This is:
o: The chance of missing depends on the missing value itself.

questions.p: A project column is skewed by a few zero scores. Which fill is most defensible?
o: The median is less affected by outliers.

questions.p: What does df.dropna(axis=1) do?
o: Fills missing values with column means
Removes only rows that are entirely empty

questions.p: What does thresh control in dropna?
o: The percentage of rows to fill
The value used to fill missing cells
The maximum number of rows to remove
The minimum number of non-null values to keep
Rows or columns below the threshold are dropped.

questions.p: In Y = f(X) + error, what does the error term capture?
o: The difference between training and test loss
The features left out of the training set
The slope of the fitted regression line
The slide defines it that way.

questions.p: Predicting whether a tumour is benign or malignant is:
o: The response lies in a finite set of classes.

questions.p: What is the zero-one loss when the predicted class equals the true class?
o: It incurs 1 only when they differ.

questions.p: Risk is best defined as:
o: The squared distance of one prediction
The loss on a single observation
The average loss on the training set
The expected loss over the data distribution

questions.p: The regression function at X = x is:
o: It is the conditional average, and it minimizes mean squared error.

questions.p: Why does prediction error remain even if we knew f exactly?
o: The training set can never be large enough
At each x there is a distribution of possible Y values
That spread is the irreducible error.
The model class is always too simple

questions.p: Which method is unsupervised on the slides?
o: PCA learns structure with no response variable.

questions.p: Which term is an expectation over the true distribution?
o: Training loss is a sample average; loss and error apply to one point.

questions.p: The learner is defined as the function in class G that:
o: Fits only the test sample exactly
True risk is unavailable, so training loss is minimized.

questions.p: A model has zero training loss but poor predictions on new data. This is:
o: Poor generalization despite minimal training loss.

questions.p: What makes test loss an unbiased estimate of generalization risk?
o: The test sample is larger than training
The test loss is always lower
The test sample uses a different distribution
The test sample is separate from training
It must be independent of the training data.

questions.p: If the test set is used for model selection, what else is needed?
o: A third set for final testing
The slide calls for a third set once selection uses the second.

questions.p: Why is least-squares linear regression convex?
o: It uses a sigmoid activation function
Its objective is quadratic in the parameters
A quadratic objective ensures a single global minimum.
Its loss is computed on test data
It always has a Hessian of zero

questions.p: What simplifies the search in a convex optimization problem?
o: The feasible set can be any non-convex shape
The function has several saddle points
The gradient is zero at every point
Every local minimum is also a global minimum
That is the defining benefit of convex problems.

questions.p: In which direction does the gradient point?
The Hessian matrix contains:
For f(x) = x² - 4x + 4 with the constraint x <= 1, where is the minimum?
o: The unconstrained minimum at 2 is infeasible, and f decreases up to x = 1.

questions.p: Which statement matches the slide comparison?
o: Gradient descent needs the inverse Hessian
Gradient descent needs only the gradient.

questions.p: Why does Newton's method struggle on very large problems?
o: It cannot use gradient information at all
It has too many learning rates to tune
It only works when the loss is non-convex
Computing and inverting the Hessian becomes infeasible
That cost grows quickly with the number of variables.

questions.p: In x_new = x_old - alpha grad f(x_old), alpha is the:
If MSE is 25, what is the RMSE?
o: RMSE is the square root of MSE.

questions.p: High training error and high test error indicate:
o: The model is too simple to capture the pattern.

questions.p: High variance means the model is:
o: Too sensitive to the training set
High variance means it captures random noise.

questions.p: Train error 1%, test error 11%. The diagnosis is:
o: Low train error with a large gap to test error.

questions.p: Train error 15%, test error 16%. The diagnosis is:
o: High train error with almost no gap.

questions.p: P(Y=0|x) = 0.10, P(Y=1|x) = 0.70, P(Y=2|x) = 0.20. The optimal classifier under zero-one loss returns:
o: No class, because there is no certainty
It picks the class with the highest conditional probability.

questions.p: Why can even the optimal classifier not reach zero error?
o: Its training set is always too small
That remaining error is the Bayes error rate.

questions.p: In the dog, cat and possum matrix, what is the misclassification error?
For class Dog in the matrix, what is fp?
Where do false negatives for class j appear?
o: In row j, off the diagonal
Actual j predicted as something else.
Outside row j and column j
In column j, off the diagonal

questions.p: For class Cat, recall is:
For class Cat, precision is:
What does specificity measure?
o: Of all non-j objects, how many were rejected
Of everything called j, how many are j
The share of all predictions that are correct
Of all real j objects, how many were found

questions.p: Which classifier suits the secure facility, and why?
o: Classifier 1, since false positives are costly
The accuracies are nearly equal; precision decides.
Classifier 2, since it admits more people
Classifier 1, since its accuracy is far higher
Classifier 2, since its recall is higher

questions.p: For true {a, b} and predicted {b, c}, multilabel accuracy is:
Exact match ratio counts an object as correct only when:
o: The whole predicted set equals the true set
More than half of the labels are right
At least one predicted label is right
The predicted set is inside the true set

questions.p: A spam filter must never send real email to junk. Which metric matters most for the spam class?
o: A false positive sends real email to junk.
Specificity of the non-spam class only

questions.p: True labels {a, b}, predicted {b, c}. What are precision and recall?
o: One correct of two predicted and of two actual.

questions.p: A feature has three categories. One-hot encoding as on the slide produces:
What is the main drawback of label encoding on a nominal feature?
o: It introduces an order that may not exist
It always creates too many columns

questions.p: What does the logistic function do?
o: The logit does the reverse mapping.
Maps probabilities to the whole real line
Rounds scores to the nearest integer
Sums the feature values to one

questions.p: The logit of p is:
At p = 0.5, what is the logit?
Why is the log-likelihood used?
o: It changes which parameters are best
It turns products of probabilities into sums
It simplifies computation and improves stability.
It turns the model into a linear regression
It removes the need for training data

questions.p: Why are both num and Target dropped from X?
o: Target comes from num, so num would leak the answer
Keeping num would reveal the label.
Pandas cannot process those two columns

questions.p: What does model.score(X_test, y_test) return for logistic regression?
o: The slide notes the variable name is misleading.

questions.p: In a classification report, support means:
o: The number of actual occurrences of each class
The number of predictions per class

questions.p: What is wrong with scaling the whole dataset before splitting?
o: Test rows influence the mean and standard deviation.

The features lose their column names

questions.p: What automatically applies the fit-on-training rule in cross-validation?
o: The fit_transform call on all data

questions.p: Which scaler is least sensitive to outliers?
o: It uses the median and IQR.

questions.p: What does an embedding model produce?
o: A database row for each pixel
Objects become vectors so that similarity can be computed.
A sorted list of class labels
A single probability for each object

questions.p: Why was NumPy far faster than a list in the slide test?
o: Lists cannot store more than 1,000 items
It stores data in a Python dictionary
It skips some elements when summing
Its internals are optimized and C-based
The slide gives C-based processing as the reason.

questions.p: What is the dot product of [2, 3, 4] and [1, 0, -1]?

How many elements each vector has

o: np.dot divides by the norms itself

Dividing by 1 leaves the dot product.

questions.p: Why is data standardized before PCA?
o: So the eigenvalues all equal one
So the covariance matrix becomes zero

questions.p: The diagonal of a covariance matrix holds:

questions.p: What defines an eigenvector of a matrix?

It is the largest column of the matrix

It keeps its direction under the transformation
It may be stretched, compressed or flipped along the same line.

questions.p: In PCA, the eigenvector with the largest eigenvalue is:

That is the first principal component.
The direction capturing the least variance
The original feature with the largest mean

questions.p: With eigenvalues 3.9566, 0.0338, 0.0079, 0.0016, what share does PC1 explain?
o: 3.9566 divided by their sum of about 4.

questions.p: What does eigenvectors[:, sorted_indices] do?

questions.p: Eigenvalues [1.01, 1.6, 3.61, 2.5] sorted descending give which indices?
PC1 for a student is computed as:

questions.p: Why is tuning a model on the test set a problem?
